messages.subject: Set up plotting region
parts:
In the non- ggplot2 world you can set up a plotting region without displaying the plot.

 

For example:

plot(x, y, type="n", axes=F, xlab="", ylab="")

 

Can you do this in ggplot2?

messages.author: d588a03e58ea7e7f
messages.subject: Re: Set up plotting region
parts:
On 6/15/2012 11:03 AM, Lancaster, Vicki wrote:
> In the non- ggplot2 world you can set up a plotting region without displaying the plot.
>
> For example:
> plot(x, y, type="n", axes=F, xlab="", ylab="")
>
> Can you do this in ggplot2?

Yes, but...

Typically, I've seen this idiom when a plot is set up (effectively, the
ranges of the axes are determined and how those correspond to the plot
area) and then additional data is displayed using points or lines or
some such. And then the axes are drawn on in a customized way.

ggplot2 approaches the problem differently. All the data and parts of
the plot are defined up front, and then it is drawn. "scale training",
the ggplot2 term for determining the extent of the axes (positional
scales) and other scales (shape, color, etc.) and how they relate the
data to what you see, is one of the big differences (advantages) ggplot2
has over base graphics.

That said, you can do something like what you ask.

x <- 1:10
y <- 1:10
DF <- data.frame(x,y)

ggplot(DF, aes(x,y)) + geom_blank()

geom_blank() will give you a valid plot, but without any of the data
represented on it. The data still influences the axes (which are drawn).
